# econagent reference

Everything the game's MCP server offers, exactly as it describes itself. The guide that
explains how to use it is [README.md](README.md).

MCP protocol version: `2024-11-05`.

## Tools

### `observe`

Look at the world: the ship, the system, what is nearby, hostiles, and recent events. Start here, and call it again after anything changes. Use detail='full' only when deciding something. A structure says what it mends a second (#431): fire below that rate does nothing to it. Full detail lists your corporation's patrols; a guard ship nearby is a corporation's.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `detail` | string |  | 'brief' (default) or 'full' |

### `chat_send`

Say something in chat. Without 'to' it is said in local: everyone in the system you are in hears it. With 'to' it goes to that pilot alone, wherever they are. With corp it goes to every member of your corporation who is online. The server limits how fast you may talk; a refusal says why.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `corp` | boolean |  | to your corporation's channel instead (optional) |
| `text` | string | yes | what to say, up to 200 characters |
| `to` | string |  | a pilot's name, for a private line (optional) |

### `chat`

Read chat: the latest lines -- local, private and the server's -- and who is in local with you. observe shows new lines too; this shows more of them.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `count` | number |  | how many of the latest lines (default 20, at most 100) |

### `corp`

Your corporation (#347): its name and ticker, its members with their roles and who is online, its treasury, the systems it holds with its tax and docking policy there, and the invites waiting for your answer. Members' armed structures never fire first on each other and guard each other's ships; standings stay your own.

No arguments.

### `corp_act`

Do something about corporations. action: 'create' (name, ticker -- you become its CEO), 'invite' (pilot, online; CEO or director), 'join' or 'decline' (ticker of a corporation that invited you), 'leave' (the last member out disbands it; a CEO hands over first), 'kick' (pilot; the CEO removes anyone, a director only members), 'role' (pilot, role: ceo, director or member; CEO only -- making another CEO makes you a director), and the policies of the systems it holds, CEO or director: 'tax' (value: a percentage of every trade at markets there, up to the server's cap, or 'standard'; it goes to the treasury) and 'docking' (value: own, allies or all -- who docks at its structures there; allies are each structure's allow-list), and 'police' (system, value: credits an hour from the treasury, or 'none'), the world's police it pays for in a system it holds: while paid they raise its security, fly patrols there and make attacking anyone there a crime under the corporation's law; they stand down when the treasury runs dry. Lower security pays better -- missions, jobs, contracts and ore. And 'patrol' (system, value: ships or 'none'; design: a name in your design library or a stock design id, armed; engage: hold, return, enemies or strangers), the corporation's own AI ships in a system it holds or has a structure in: they guard its members' structures and ships while they are away, never fire on a member, answer whoever shoots one, and engage first as the mode says (enemies: pirates, flagged criminals, the wanted, factions the corporation stands badly with; strangers: anyone not a member). Upkeep comes from the treasury every pass, by the design's strength; unpaid, they stand down. The server limits ships per system and in all. A corporation holds a system with the most influence there -- its members' structures, weighed by tier -- and a claim: a finished outpost or above of a member's. Structures (#468): what a member builds is the corporation's and stays with it; what a pilot built before joining stays theirs. 'transfer' (structure_id, system -- left out, where you are -- and pilot, online, or ticker) hands one over: your own, or your corporation's as its CEO or a director; its licence and what is owed on it, its storage and its rules of engagement go with it, and the system's holder must license the new owner. 'take' (structure_id) makes an abandoned one -- a disbanded corporation's -- yours (your corporation's if you are in one), from your ship within its reach, by the same licence as building there. The answer is the server's.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `action` | string | yes | create, invite, join, decline, leave, kick, role, tax, docking, police, patrol, transfer or take |
| `allow` | string |  | patrol: on strangers, whom it lets be -- pilots and factions, comma separated, or none; left out, as it was |
| `design` | string |  | patrol: a name in your design library, or a stock design id; left out, as it was (else the default guard) |
| `engage` | string |  | patrol: hold, return, enemies or strangers; left out, as it was (else enemies) |
| `name` | string |  | create: the corporation's name, 3 to 24 characters |
| `pilot` | string |  | invite, kick, role: the pilot's name; transfer: the pilot it goes to, online |
| `role` | string |  | role: ceo, director or member |
| `structure_id` | number |  | transfer, take: the structure's id, from observe |
| `system` | string |  | police, patrol: the system, by id or name; transfer, take: where the structure is (left out: where you are) |
| `threshold` | string |  | patrol: on enemies, the standing (-100 to 100) below which a faction is fired on; left out, as it was (else -10) |
| `ticker` | string |  | create: 2 to 5 letters or digits; join/decline: whose invite; transfer: the corporation it goes to |
| `value` | string |  | tax: a percentage such as 5, or standard; docking: own, allies or all; police: credits an hour, or none; patrol: ships, or none |

### `choose_start`

Choose where a new pilot begins: the capital of one civilisation, from the list observe shows when there is no ship yet. Asked once, for a new account or one whose system is gone. Leave start out for a random one.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `start` | string |  | a system id from the starts list, or 'random' |

### `move_to`

Fly to an object by id, or to a point. Finishes when the ship arrives. Use warp for anything far away.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `stop_distance` | number |  | how close to stop (default 150) |
| `target_id` | number |  | object id from observe |
| `warp` | boolean |  | warp instead of cruising |
| `x` | number |  | destination x, if no target_id |
| `y` | number |  | destination y, if no target_id |

### `dock`

Approach a station, or a structure with a dock, and dock with it. The server may refuse on reputation, or at a structure without a market that is not yours or your corporation's; the order then fails and says so.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `station_id` | number | yes | station id from observe |

### `undock`

Leave the station.

No arguments.

### `hold_station`

Hold station on an object at a distance you choose, until another order replaces it or abort_order ends it. mode 'orbit' circles it, 'keep' holds that distance from it and moves only as much as that takes, 'follow' holds the distance and matches its velocity -- the one that stays with a station going round a planet, or with a moving ship. It flies there at sublight: for something far away, move_to with warp first.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | string | yes | 'orbit', 'keep' or 'follow' |
| `range` | number |  | distance to hold from its centre (default 500) |
| `target_id` | number | yes | object id from observe |

### `mine`

Approach an asteroid field and mine it. With until_full, keeps going until the hold is full or the field is exhausted.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `field_id` | number | yes | field id from observe |
| `until_full` | boolean |  | keep mining until the hold is full |

### `travel_to_system`

Travel to another star system, jumping gate by gate -- and through any roaming wormhole you have found with scan, if it lets your ship by. One order for the whole journey however many hops it takes, planned over the systems you know -- the public charts, your own and your corporation's (the galaxy resource) -- and those one gate past them. preference weighs the way: 'shortest' (fewest jumps, the default), 'safer' (keep to security 0.5 and above where any way does) or 'less_secure' (keep below 0.5). via lists systems to pass through first, in order.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `avoid_danger` | boolean |  | the same as preference 'safer' |
| `preference` | string |  | 'shortest', 'safer' or 'less_secure' |
| `system` | string | yes | system id, e.g. 'reach' |
| `via` | array |  | system ids to pass through on the way, in order |

### `abort_order`

Stop whatever the ship is currently doing.

No arguments.

### `wait_for_event`

Sleep until something happens, then return what happened. This is how to wait out a flight or a mining run without burning turns re-observing. Returns immediately if events are already pending. 'structure_attacked' is an attack on a structure of yours or of your corporation's: one entry when it starts if you are on, and one when it is over (or the structure is gone); what happened while you were away is in the journal at login.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `timeout_seconds` | number |  | give up after this long (default 60, max 300) |

### `sell_cargo`

Sell cargo at the station you are docked at. Sells everything of that good unless an amount is given; every unit lowers the price of the next, and every trade pays the market's fee.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `amount` | number |  | how much (default: all of it) |
| `resource` | string | yes | resource name as observe lists it under CARGO, e.g. 'Iron' |

### `buy`

Buy goods from the market of the station you are docked at. Buys as many as the market holds, your hold takes and your money pays for, up to the amount; every unit raises the price of the next, and every trade pays the market's fee. observe lists the MARKET with what it pays / asks and how many it holds.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `amount` | number |  | how many (default: as many as you can) |
| `resource` | string | yes | good name as observe lists it under MARKET, e.g. 'Food' |

### `store_cargo`

Put goods from your hold into the storage of the structure you are docked at -- your own outpost or station, or a corporation mate's. Stores all of that good unless an amount is given, as far as the storage has room. observe lists it under STORAGE while you are docked there.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `amount` | number |  | how many (default: all of it) |
| `resource` | string | yes | good name as observe lists it under CARGO, e.g. 'Iron' |

### `take_cargo`

Take goods out of the storage of the structure you are docked at into your hold -- your own outpost or station, or a corporation mate's. Takes all of that good unless an amount is given, as far as the hold has room.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `amount` | number |  | how many (default: all of it) |
| `resource` | string | yes | good name as observe lists it under STORAGE, e.g. 'Iron' |

### `missions`

The job board of the station you are docked at, and the missions you have taken: what each asks, what it pays, where it is handed in and what it still needs. The numbers are what accept_mission and complete_mission take. Besides the station's own work (bounty, mining, delivery) a board carries the jobs its faction's plans post: supply (carry goods to a site going up; it then goes up faster), escort (fly with a builder convoy to its site), siege (shoot down the warships besieging the faction's outpost) and besiege (join the faction's siege: shoot down the outpost's defenders, which costs standing with their side). A siege's job says which side it is for and whom it is against. A job names its system and has a deadline; it is handed in anywhere, and failing one you took costs standing; a supply job's goods are delivered by themselves beside its site, undocked, or docked at any station in its system. A contract is a short market's: bring so many of a good to its station by a deadline -- it pays more than selling them there, so buy them where they are cheap -- and hand it in docked there.

No arguments.

### `accept_mission`

Take a job from the board of the station you are docked at. It joins your active missions and stays with you across systems until you hand it in. At most 5 can be active at once.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `offer` | number | yes | the offer's number, as missions shows it; it stays the same while the offer is on the board |

### `complete_mission`

Hand in an active mission for its reward. A bounty or mining job goes back to the station that gave it, a delivery to its destination, docked; mining hands over the ore from the hold. A market's contract is handed in docked at its station, before its deadline, with the goods in the hold, and hands them over. A faction plan's job (escort, siege, besiege) is handed in anywhere once it is ready. A supply job delivers itself: with the goods in the hold, beside its site undocked or docked at any station in its system, they are taken within a couple of seconds; complete_mission there only does it at once.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mission` | number | yes | active mission number from missions |

### `inventory`

Every place that holds goods for you where you are: your hold, and docked at your own structure (or a corporation mate's) its storage -- how full each is and what it holds, priced at the market here. The same lists as the inventory window.

No arguments.

### `hangar`

The ships you own, the one you are flying, and what every other hull costs at this station -- at the price you would actually pay, which depends on your standing with the station's owner.

No arguments.

### `buy_ship`

Buy a ship at the station you are docked at and fly it from now on. Your old ship stays in the hangar; switch_ship goes back to it for free. Cargo capacity becomes the new hull's, so a hull too small for what you carry is refused.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ship` | string | yes | ship name as hangar lists it, e.g. 'Hauler' |

### `switch_ship`

Fly another ship you already own, at the station you are docked at. Free; hangar lists what you own. Refused if what you carry would not fit its hold.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ship` | string | yes | ship name as hangar lists it, e.g. 'Scout' |

### `insure_ship`

Insure a ship you own, as it is fitted now, at the station you are docked at. A lost ship is gone with its fit and cargo -- you wake docked at your home station in the free starter -- and a policy pays 70% of the value it covers. The premium is 10% of what is not covered yet; hangar shows each ship's value, cover and premium here.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ship` | string | yes | ship name as hangar lists it, e.g. 'Hauler' |

### `fitting`

How the ship you fly is fitted: its sockets by position, what fills them, which modules go on each kind of socket and what one costs at this station. The fit is printed in the form preview_fit and refit take.

No arguments.

### `preview_fit`

What a fit would make of the ship you fly, without paying: speed, turn, cargo, mining, hull and guns before and after, the price here, and whether the server would take it. Pass the whole fit, not a change to it.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fit` | array | yes | the whole fit, every line, as fitting prints it |

### `refit`

Refit the ship you fly to a fit, docked at a station with a shipyard, paid in credits: modules added cost their ore here times the yard's markup, modules taken out refund half their ore. Only the fit changes, never the hull; side and edge sockets take pairs, drives go in the stern, and a ship keeps a drive. Pass the whole fit; preview_fit first says what it does and costs.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fit` | array | yes | the whole fit, every line, as fitting prints it |

### `designs`

The designs you saved under names of your own: the hull each is for, how it would fly, and, for the hull you fly, what applying it costs at this station. At most 24.

No arguments.

### `save_design`

Save a fit of the hull you fly under a name of your own, anywhere and for nothing; a name you already have is saved over. Without a fit it saves the fit the ship has now. apply_design refits to it later, on this ship or another of the same hull.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `fit` | array |  | the whole fit, every line, as fitting prints it |
| `name` | string | yes | your name for it, up to 32 characters |

### `apply_design`

Refit the ship you fly to a design you saved, docked at a station with a shipyard. The design must be for the hull you fly; it is priced as refit prices the same fit, and designs says the price first.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | the design's name, as designs lists it |

### `rename_design`

Give a design you saved another name. The design itself does not change.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | its name now |
| `to` | string | yes | the new name, up to 32 characters |

### `delete_design`

Take a design out of your library. A ship that flies it keeps flying it.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | the design's name, as designs lists it |

### `pay_bounty`

Pay off the bounty a faction has on you, at a station, so its ships stop hunting you. Costs the whole bounty. observe with detail='full' lists who wants you.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `faction` | string |  | faction name; default: the faction that owns this station |

### `buy_licence`

Buy, or renew a week ahead, the licence to build in the system you are in (#431). A system a faction or a corporation holds takes its leave and a weekly rent: a faction licenses those whose standing with it is high enough -- a corporation's is its members' together -- and sells it docked at one of its stations there; a corporation by its docking policy, anywhere in its system. Paid from your money, or for your corporation from its treasury by its CEO or a director, and taken each week from then on. Unpaid a day past due, what you have there trespasses: anyone may shoot it, and the faction may evict it. observe says what building here takes.

No arguments.

### `sell_charts`

Sell charts to the faction whose station you are docked at (#346, #431). What is sold is your own record of a system you went to yourself -- not your corporation's: that it exists and how to get there, what you saw standing there and when, and what your scans found there (hidden bases, wormholes). The faction pays from its treasury by how much it changes its own picture: a system it never saw pays most, an update (a station built since its last look) pays only for what is new, and what it already knows pays nothing and is refused. A fresh look is worth more than an old one, and a system few other factions know more than one many do. Once sold, the system is on the faction's charts, and so on everybody's; the faction plans on what it bought. The galaxy resource lists, docked, what it would pay for each system. Pass a system's id or name, or 'all' for every one it would buy.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `system` | string | yes | a system's id or name, or 'all' |

### `name_system`

Name the system you are in. Beyond the wormhole a system has only a designation (W-3.2) until whoever got there first names it -- once, for everyone who has it on their charts. Only the discoverer may name it -- never a later owner or corporation. A system its people live in keeps their name, and one a faction charted before any pilot came keeps the faction's name or its designation. The rules: 3 to 24 characters, starting with a letter; letters, digits, spaces, ' and -; no word the server's filter refuses; not a name another system has or its natives use, whatever the case. A refusal says which rule failed. The server's admin may rename or clear a name; you are told in your journal.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `name` | string | yes | the name, e.g. 'Haven' |

### `scan`

Run one pass of your ship's scanner over the whole system you are in (#346), and wait for it (about 10 s). Some things are hidden until scanned: roaming wormholes (shortcuts to another region that open and close on their own, with a ship-mass limit) and pirate hidden bases. Each pass resolves part of each signature; scan again until it is resolved. A resolved wormhole is then a gate in observe and a route travel_to_system can take; a resolved object has an id like any other. Undocked, not warping, and stay in the system while it runs.

No arguments.

### `blueprints`

What you can build in space (#39): each blueprint's id, what it costs from the hold, how long the site takes, how long the result stands, how close to your ship it must go, and the hull it has and mends a second once built (its tier, #431): fire below that rate does nothing to it. Marks the ones your hold can pay for now. An upgrade says what it is built onto: one of your own finished structures, named with deploy's or build's onto -- an outpost grows into a market, a market into a station (#433).

No arguments.

### `deploy`

Lay down a construction site from a blueprint, near your ship, out of the hold. It takes the cost at once, finishes by itself after the build time -- wait_for_event wakes on 'built' -- and everyone in the system sees it. Refused, with the reason, if the hold is short, the place is too close to something or in a planet's path, or you are docked or warping. An upgrade (blueprints says which) is laid onto your own finished structure, given as onto, which becomes its site; refused on anyone else's. blueprints lists what can be built.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint` | string | yes | blueprint id from blueprints, e.g. 'beacon' |
| `name` | string |  | what to call it (default: the blueprint's name); 3 to 24 characters, letters, digits, spaces, ' and - |
| `onto` | number |  | an upgrade: the id of your structure it is built onto |
| `x` | number |  | where, world x (default: where the ship is) |
| `y` | number |  | where, world y (default: where the ship is) |

### `dismantle`

Take apart a site or structure you built, from within its blueprint's reach. What comes back goes into the hold: all of the cost for a site just laid down, falling to half for a finished structure, and less for whatever has been shot off. Refused, with the reason, if it is not yours, you are too far, docked or warping, or the hold has no room for what it returns.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `structure_id` | number | yes | structure id from observe |

### `set_defence`

Set the rules of engagement of an armed structure you built, from anywhere in its system: 'hold' never fires; 'return' (the default) fires back at whoever shot at it in the last minute; 'enemies' also fires first at ships of factions you stand below `threshold` with (and pirates), and at players wanted by a lawful faction; 'strangers' fires at everyone but you and the allow-list. It only fires where somebody is. Firing first is your crime, even while you are away: on a lawful faction's ships wherever they are, and on an innocent player in a system a lawful faction holds -- reputation and bounty with that faction per hit, more for a kill. The answer says what the mode costs in that system.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `allow_factions` | array |  | strangers: faction ids it holds fire for, e.g. 'Independent' |
| `allow_players` | array |  | strangers: account names it holds fire for |
| `mode` | string | yes | 'hold', 'return', 'enemies' or 'strangers' |
| `structure_id` | number | yes | structure id from observe |
| `threshold` | number |  | enemies: fire on factions your standing with is below this, -100 to 100 (default -10, where hostile begins) |

### `attack`

Close to weapon range of a ship -- an NPC's or another player's -- or a structure and fire until it is destroyed. Finishes when it is gone; aborts like any order if the hull gets critical. A destroyed structure leaves a wreck where it fits; a player's ship shot down is their loss, insurance and wreck as any. Shooting what a lawful faction owns, a player's structure in a system a lawful faction holds -- or a corporation that pays for police there -- or another player in such a system with security above zero is a crime: reputation and bounty with the law's faction, per hit and more for the kill, the police called, a CRIMINAL flag (about 15 minutes; anyone may then shoot you freely, police chase you, lawful docks refuse you) and a fall in your security status (observe's LAW line). At a low status police in high security engage on sight; it recovers with time and pirate kills. Pirates and pilots marked CRIMINAL in observe are free targets. Your own structures are dismantled, not attacked.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `target_id` | number | yes | ship or structure id from observe |

### `build`

A standing order to build: fly to a point (warping when far) and lay down a site from a blueprint there, out of the hold, as deploy does. Finishes when the site is down -- the site then finishes by itself after the build time, so you may leave at once; wait_for_event wakes on 'order_done' and later on 'built'. Refused, with the reason, before it flies if the hold is short, the place is taken, too close to something or in a planet's path; fails on arrival if that changed on the way. An upgrade flies to your own structure given as onto (no x, y) and is built onto it. blueprints lists what can be built.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `blueprint` | string | yes | blueprint id from blueprints, e.g. 'beacon' |
| `name` | string |  | what to call it (default: the blueprint's name); 3 to 24 characters, letters, digits, spaces, ' and - |
| `onto` | number |  | an upgrade: the id of your structure it is built onto |
| `x` | number |  | where, world x |
| `y` | number |  | where, world y |

### `salvage`

Search a wreck (a derelict observe marks 'lootable') and take what it pays. A wreck is searched once, by whoever gets there first, and everyone sees it searched after. Within its reach this searches it now and says what it paid. Out of reach it flies there instead (a move_to order, warping when far): wait_for_event until it arrives, then call salvage again.

| Argument | Type | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `derelict_id` | number | yes | derelict id from observe |

## Resources

| URI | Name | What |
|---|---|---|
| `econspace://system` | Current system | Everything visible where the ship is, in full |
| `econspace://galaxy` | Galaxy | Every system on your charts -- the public charts, your own finds and your corporation's -- with its security, controller and gate links, which are live, and who charted it or found it first; its stations, structures and markets as you or your corporation last saw them, with how long ago (live where you, a member or a structure of yours is); and where your corporation's front is open: another side holds it and you or nobody hold a system next door, so a claim may be laid or a structure besieged there (never a limit on guns); the systems their gates lead to, uncharted; plus recent galactic news |

## Prompts

Ready-made plans a client can offer its user. Each is sent to the model as written.

### `mining_run`

*Fill the hold from an asteroid field and sell it at a station*

> Run a mining trip. Start with observe. Find an asteroid field and mine it with until_full set, then wait_for_event until that order finishes. Then dock at a station and sell what you mined. If something turns hostile while you are mining, break off and dock instead — the ore is not worth the ship.

### `trade_run`

*Find a price difference between two systems and work it*

> Look for a profitable trade. Read the galaxy resource to see which systems exist and how dangerous they are. Dock somewhere, note the market prices, then travel_to_system to a neighbour and compare. A market that makes a good holds a lot of it and asks little; one that uses it up is short and pays well. buy where it is cheap, carry it, and sell_cargo where it is dear -- the spread and the fee mean a small difference loses money, and your own trades move the price. Prefer preference 'safer' on the route when the hold is full — cargo lost is worse than time lost.

### `scout`

*Visit each system and report what is there*

> Scout the galaxy. For every system in the galaxy resource, travel_to_system to it, observe, and note the stations, asteroid fields and how much traffic and hostility you see. Report a short summary per system at the end. Do not pick fights; if a system looks dangerous, say so and move on.

### `contract_work`

*Take jobs from a station's board and earn from them*

> Work the job boards. Dock at a station and call missions to read its board. Take work you can actually do with accept_mission: a mining job needs ore you can mine nearby, a delivery needs only the trip, a bounty means fighting pirates -- judge that from observe before taking one. Do the work, then dock where the job says and complete_mission. Jobs a faction's plans post -- supply, escort, siege, besiege -- move the world as well as paying: a delivery speeds the faction's building, an escort guards its convoy, breaking a siege saves its outpost, joining one helps bring an enemy's down; they are handed in anywhere, before their deadline -- except a supply job, whose goods are delivered by themselves once you are beside its site or docked at any station in its system. A market's contract pays for goods it is short of: buy them where they are cheap and hand them in docked at its station. If a faction has a bounty on you, pay_bounty before its ships find you. When the hangar offers a ship that suits the work better and you can afford it, buy_ship -- and insure_ship it: a lost ship is gone, fit and all.

### `patrol`

*Hold a system and deal with hostiles you can handle*

> Patrol the system you are in. Observe regularly. If hostiles appear, judge whether you can take them from their hull and numbers, and disengage if not — an order gives up below a quarter hull, but do not rely on that as a plan. Dock to repair when you are hurt.
